# Rashtriya Sanatan Sanskar Seva Sansthan (Trust) — Comprehensive Knowledge Base
Official Site: https://rashtriyasanatantrust.in/
Legal Identity: Public Charitable & Religious Trust under Indian Trusts Act, 1882
Core Classification: Hindu Sanatan Dharma Trust (सनातन धर्म न्यास)
Pillars: राष्ट्र हित ! • सनातन हित !! • परिवार हित !!! (Nation Welfare, Sanatan Values, Family Upliftment)

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Identity
Rashtriya Sanatan Sanskar Seva Sansthan (Trust) is a pan-India Hindu religious and charitable organization. The Trust operates to restore, teach, and facilitate the authentic Vedic 16 Sanskars across society, counter cultural disconnect, and build a unified, morally conscious Sanatani society. It bridges traditional Vedic spiritual heritage with active grassroots social welfare, including labor advocacy, cow welfare (Gau Seva), and assistance for underprivileged families.

While the registered national headquarters is situated in Uttar Pradesh, India, the Trust serves Sanatani families across the country and globally through publications, virtual counseling, local convenors, and community welfare programs.

---

## 2. Core Missions & Programs

### A. The 16 Vedic Sanskars (षोडश संस्कार)
In Sanatan Dharma, human life is sanctified through 16 spiritual milestones (Sanskars) that purify mind, body, and soul:
1. Garbhadhana (गर्भाधान): Conscious, sanctified conception prayer invoking noble progeny.
2. Pumsavana (पुंसवन): Rites performed during early pregnancy to bless the health and vitality of the fetus.
3. Simantonnayana (सीमन्तोन्नयन): Ceremony ensuring mental serenity, protection, and positive environment for the expectant mother.
4. Jatakarma (जातकर्म): Post-birth ritual offering honey and ghee with Vedic mantras blessing intellectual wisdom (medha) and longevity.
5. Namakarana (नामकरण): Naming ceremony giving the newborn an auspicious, astrologically and spiritually sound name.
6. Nishkramana (निष्क्रमण): Taking the infant outdoors for the first time to perceive nature, Sun (Surya), and Moon (Chandra).
7. Annaprashana (अन्नप्राशन): First sacred feeding of solid, wholesome food (kheer/grains).
8. Chudakarana / Mundan (चूड़ाकर्म): First head tonsure promoting cleanliness, neurological stimulation, and shedding prenatal impressions.
9. Karnavedha (कर्णवेध): Piercing of earlobes for acupuncture benefits, intellect enhancement, and ornamentation.
10. Vidyarambha / Akshararambha (विद्यारंभ): Initiation into alphabets, Saraswati Vandana, and the joy of formal learning.
11. Upanayana / Yajnopavita (उपनयन / जनेऊ): Sacred thread investiture, Gayatri Mantra initiation, and birth into spiritual consciousness (Dvija).
12. Vedarambha (वेदारंभ): Formal commencement of studying the Vedas and sacred Hindu scriptures under Guru guidance.
13. Keshanta / Godana (केशांत): Marking maturity, adulthood discipline, and charity.
14. Samavartana (समावर्तन): Academic graduation signifying the end of student life (Brahmacharya) and transition to family responsibilities.
15. Vivaha (विवाह): Sacred, indissoluble matrimony unifying two souls before Agni Devata to uphold Dharma, Artha, Kama, and Moksha.
16. Antyeshti (अन्त्येष्टि): Final farewell Vedic fire rites honoring the departed soul and commending it to Paramatma.

The Sansthan provides free scriptural manuals, guides families with qualified Vedic scholars, and assists economically weaker families with free ceremonial arrangements.

### B. The 12 Family Principles (हमारा द्वादश आग्रह)
The Trust encourages every Hindu household to practice 12 daily life ideals:
1. Nitya Sandhya & Gayatri Japa (दैनिक संध्या एवं गायत्री जप)
2. Gau Seva & First Roti to Gau Mata (गौ सेवा व पहली रोटी गाय को)
3. Tulsi & Surya Arghya (तुलसी पूजन व सूर्य अर्घ्य)
4. Reading Sacred Scriptures at Home (घर में गीता, रामायण का पठन)
5. Traditional Mother Tongue & Devanagari Use (मातृभाषा व संस्कार)
6. Swadeshi & Self-Reliance (स्वदेशी व आत्मनिर्भरता)
7. Cleanliness & Deva Sthal Purity (स्वच्छता एवं मंदिर शुद्धि)
8. Family Dining with Gratitude Mantra (सपरिवार भोजन व प्रार्थना)
9. Respect for Elders and Parents (मातृ-पितृ पूजन व वंदन)
10. Abstinence from Intoxicants & Immorality (व्यसनमुक्ति व सदाचार)
11. Supporting Needy & Unorganized Workers (दीन-दुखियों की सहायता)
12. Nation First in All Thoughts and Deeds (राष्ट्र सर्वोपरि की भावना)

### C. Gau Seva & Protection (गौ संरक्षण एवं संवर्धन)
- Supporting indigenous cow shelters (Gaushalas).
- Emergency medical aid for abandoned or injured bovines.
- Educating rural communities on organic farming and the spiritual and medical potency of Panchagavya.

### D. Shramik Kalyan & Grassroots Labor Welfare (श्रमिक कल्याण)
- Conducting awareness camps for unorganized daily wage laborers and construction workers.
- Registration drives for central and state government schemes (e-Shram, PM-SYM, Atal Pension, educational scholarships).
- Legal counseling and moral support for working-class families.

## 4. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q: What makes Rashtriya Sanatan Sanskar Seva Sansthan distinct from regional trusts?
A: It is an all-India Hindu Sanatan Dharma Trust combining authentic Vedic sacramental rites (16 Sanskars) with grassroots labor empowerment, nationwide member outreach, and strict financial transparency.

Q: How can devotees donate?
A: Devotees can contribute directly through the verified Bank of India account or UPI QR code available on https://rashtriyasanatantrust.in/donate. Instant digital receipts with tamper-evident serial numbers are issued.

Q: Are donations tax exempt?
A: Yes, the Trust operates under the Indian Trusts Act and fulfills 12A & 80G tax-exempt philanthropic requirements.

Q: Can individuals outside Uttar Pradesh join?
A: Absolutely. Any Sanatani citizen in India or worldwide can register as an Annual Member (₹200/year) or Volunteer via the website to participate in ideological propagation and social initiatives.
